sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Mac Cuill was an Irish god. He was the husband of the land goddess Banba. His name meant Son of Holly, a plant associated with winter, which suggests a link to that season. With his brothers Mac Cécht and Mac Gréine he belonged to a trio of parallel gods. Each brother was the consort of one of the three important land goddesses. Koch calls him Etar Mac Cuill, Son of Hazel.
